html:
A castle on the Gold Coast, begun as a wooden lodge by the Swedish Africa Company in 1653 and held by the English from 1664, who made it their headquarters on the coast.

It was one of about forty forts and castles that Europeans built along this short coast to buy gold and captives. Its underground dungeons held hundreds of people at a time before they were shipped to the Americas in the Atlantic slave trade. It was the seat of British rule until the capital moved to Accra in 1877. With Elmina and the other forts it became a World Heritage Site in 1979, and it draws many visitors of the African diaspora. See also the Royal African Company.
